_comment: The achievement set, and the map from our own keys to the ids Play
Games and Game Center hand back.
HOW TO FILL IN THE IDS
1. Create each achievement below in Play Console -> Play Games
Services -> Achievements. Use the name, description and points
verbatim, or the Console and this file stop agreeing.
2. Download the resources zip from that page (Play Console gives you
a `res` folder containing games-ids.xml) and drop games-ids.xml
into android/app/src/main/res/values/. That file is what the Play
Games SDK itself reads.
3. Copy each id out of games-ids.xml into `androidId` here. They look
like CgkIxxxxxxxxxxEAIQAQ. The Dart side cannot read an Android
string resource, so this is not duplication for its own sake — the
plugin takes the literal id.
4. iOS: create the same set in App Store Connect and put its
identifiers in `iosId`. Game Center lets you choose those, so the
`key` below is a sensible thing to reuse.
An achievement with a blank id is simply skipped — no crash, no error.
That is what makes it safe to ship this file before the Console work is
done, and it is why the code never assumes an id exists.
POINTS: 5 at the low end, 50 at the high end, graded by how much play
each one actually costs. This is a budget, not a score. Play Games caps
the total across a game — Google documents 1000 — and that cap does not
grow when the campaign does. These fourteen spend 295, so a campaign
that goes to ten thousand levels still has room for the milestones it
will want. `achievements_test.dart` holds the ceiling and the 5..50
range, because the failure mode is not a wrong number today: it is
discovering three years in that the budget is gone.

achievements.name: Three Star Job
achievements.description: Earn three stars on a level.

achievements.name: Whitewash
achievements.description: Win a match holding 95% of the board.

achievements.name: Overtime
achievements.description: Win a match in sudden death.

achievements.name: Frontier
achievements.description: Deploy a unit in the opponent's half.
